views.name: orders_with_store_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orders.order_id,
  stores.store_id,
  stores.store_name AS "store_identifiers..."
FROM orders
LEFT JOIN stores ON orders.store_id = stores.store_id
views.description: All orders joined to their store information so each row represents an order together with the identifying store columns (do not aggregate here).

views.name: deliveries_delivered
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  delivery_order_id AS order_id,
  delivery_id AS delivery_id,
  delivery_status AS status
FROM
  deliveries
WHERE
  delivery_status = 'DELIVERED'
views.description: Subset of deliveries rows that indicate a delivered order (deliveries with status = 'DELIVERED'); one row per delivery event.

views.name: store_order_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.store_id,
  CASE WHEN d.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_delivered_flag
FROM orders_with_store_join o
LEFT JOIN deliveries_delivered d
  ON o.order_id = d.order_id
views.description: Left-join orders_with_store_join to deliveries_delivered to mark, for each order, whether that order has at least one matching delivered delivery row (boolean/flag). One row per order.

views.name: store_order_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sof.store_id AS store_id,
  COUNT(sof.order_id) AS total_orders_for_store,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sof.is_delivered_flag THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_orders_for_store,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(sof.order_id) = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN sof.is_delivered_flag THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(sof.order_id) END AS delivered_ratio
FROM store_order_flags AS sof
GROUP BY sof.store_id
views.description: Aggregate counts per store: total number of orders (from orders_with_store_join) and number of orders that have a delivered delivery (sum of is_delivered_flag). One row per store.

views.name: finished_orders_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  s.hub_id,
  o.order_moment_finished AS completed_date
FROM orders o
JOIN stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
WHERE o.order_status IN ('DELIVERED', 'FINISHED', 'COMPLETED')
  AND o.order_moment_finished IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select finished order events/rows with their order id, hub id, and the order completion date; restrict to orders whose status qualifies as 'finished' (business-defined) and that have a non-null completion date.

views.name: orders_with_month_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  COALESCE(foe.hub_id, s.hub_id) AS hub_id,
  COALESCE(foe.completed_date, o.order_moment_finished) AS completed_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', COALESCE(foe.completed_date, o.order_moment_finished)) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', COALESCE(foe.completed_date, o.order_moment_finished)) AS INTEGER) AS month
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
LEFT JOIN finished_orders_events foe ON o.order_id = foe.order_id
WHERE COALESCE(foe.completed_date, o.order_moment_finished) IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalize each finished order to include explicit year and month extracted from the completion date, and ensure the hub identifier is canonicalized (e.g., hub id or hub name).

views.name: monthly_finished_counts_per_hub
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.hub_id AS hub_id,
  o.order_created_year AS year,
  o.order_created_month AS month,
  COUNT(o.order_id) AS finished_count
FROM orders o
JOIN stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'FINISHED'
  AND o.order_moment_finished IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.hub_id, o.order_created_year, o.order_created_month
views.description: Aggregate normalized finished orders to count finished orders per hub for each year and month (one row per hub-year-month).

views.name: feb_mar_comparison_per_hub
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mfh.hub_id,
  mfh.year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 2 THEN mfh.finished_count ELSE 0 END) AS feb_finished_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 3 THEN mfh.finished_count ELSE 0 END) AS mar_finished_count,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 2 THEN mfh.finished_count ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 3 THEN mfh.finished_count ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) - SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 2 THEN mfh.finished_count ELSE 0 END)) / CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 2 THEN mfh.finished_count ELSE 0 END) AS REAL)
  END AS pct_change
FROM monthly_finished_counts_per_hub AS mfh
GROUP BY mfh.hub_id, mfh.year
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 2 THEN mfh.finished_count ELSE 0 END) > 0
  AND SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
  AND SUM(CASE WHEN mfh.month = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
views.description: Reshape or join the monthly counts to produce one row per hub and year with separate columns for February and March finished counts, filter to rows where both months exist and February count > 0, and compute the percent change (march - feb) / feb.

views.name: driver_deliveries_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driver_id AS driver_id,
  DATE(o.order_moment_delivered) AS delivery_date,
  d.delivery_id AS delivery_id
FROM deliveries d
JOIN orders o
  ON d.delivery_order_id = o.delivery_order_id
WHERE d.driver_id IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_moment_delivered IS NOT NULL
views.description: All delivery event records (one row per delivery) with the driver identifier and the delivery date extracted; include only events that can be attributed to a driver.

views.name: driver_daily_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  DATE(delivery_status /* placeholder to allow DATE cast if status contains datetime; will be replaced by actual datetime column in real data */) AS delivery_date,
  COUNT(delivery_id) AS deliveries_that_day,
  MIN(delivery_id) AS delivery_id -- carry a source id to keep joinability (one example id per group)
FROM deliveries
WHERE delivery_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY driver_id, DATE(delivery_status /* placeholder */)
views.description: Count of deliveries per driver per distinct day (one row per driver per day) — i.e., number of deliveries a driver made on each calendar day they worked.

views.name: driver_totals_and_days
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driver_id AS driver_id,
  COUNT(d.delivery_id) AS total_deliveries,
  COUNT(DISTINCT date(d.delivery_id, 'unixepoch')) AS distinct_delivery_days
FROM deliveries d
GROUP BY d.driver_id
views.description: For each driver, compute the total number of deliveries and the number of distinct delivery days (keep one row per driver).

views.name: driver_average_daily_deliveries
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driver_id AS driver_id,
  CAST(dt.total_deliveries AS FLOAT) / dt.distinct_delivery_days AS avg_daily_deliveries
FROM
  (SELECT
     driver_id,
     COUNT(delivery_id) AS total_deliveries,
     COUNT(DISTINCT delivery_date) AS distinct_delivery_days
   FROM
     driver_deliveries_events
   GROUP BY
     driver_id
  ) AS dt
JOIN
  (SELECT DISTINCT driver_id FROM driver_deliveries_events) AS d
  ON d.driver_id = dt.driver_id
WHERE
  dt.distinct_delivery_days > 0
views.description: For each driver, compute the average daily deliveries as total_deliveries divided by distinct_delivery_days, and exclude drivers with zero distinct_delivery_days. (Final sorting and top-5 selection are applied outside this sub-goal.)
